title: Consortium
standfirst: Eleven beneficiaries across seven countries, coordinated by Rheinland-Pfälzische Technische Universität Kaiserslautern-Landau (RPTU).

items.name: RHEINLAND-PFALZISCHE TECHNISCHE UNIVERSITAT
items.in_triad: Coordinates the project and leads project management, ethics and data governance (WP11, WP12). Also leads the systematic review of pedagogical models and the cross-country analysis of the pilot results.
items.brings: Cognitive science, developmental psychology and diagnostics, with expertise in how digital environments affect skills, in usability, and in ethical, legal and social questions.

items.name: VILNIAUS GEDIMINO TECHNIKOS UNIVERSITETAS
items.in_triad: Leads the co-creation of pedagogical patterns and classroom scenarios with schools (WP2), and the project's communication, dissemination and stakeholder engagement (WP9, WP10).
items.brings: Scientific literacy, digital communication, citizen engagement and citizen science, and co-creative methods for working with varied groups of stakeholders.

items.name: HOCHSCHULE RUHR WEST
items.in_triad: Leads the review of pedagogical models, competences and AI tools that the framework is built on (WP1), and the professional development modules for teachers.
items.brings: Artificial intelligence, computer science and digital competence research, with experience in systematic reviews and education technology.

items.name: JYVÄSKYLÄN YLIOPISTO
items.in_triad: Leads the EU-wide classroom pilots in six countries (WP5).
items.brings: ICT use, innovative learning environments and digital well-being, with a focus on how AI tools affect motivation and technostress.

items.name: ELLINOGERMANIKI AGOGI SCHOLI PANAGEA SAVVA AE
items.in_triad: Leads the pre-test pilots of the classroom scenarios in Croatia, Germany and Greece (WP4), and brings the view from everyday school practice.
items.brings: Long-standing experience in designing educational scenarios and bringing digital tools into classrooms. A bridge between research and practice.

items.name: UNIVERSITEIT GENT
items.in_triad: Leads the neuroscientific studies on engagement and learning with AI-supported tools (WP3).
items.brings: Virtual and augmented reality learning environments, social robotics, soundscapes and biomonitoring, for both behavioural and physiological insight.

items.name: QUANTIA CONSULTING SRL
items.in_triad: Leads the harmonisation and enrichment of the pilot data and the interactive dashboard (WP7), and the policy handover at the end of the project.
items.brings: Data engineering, advanced analytics, decision-support systems and FAIR data management.

items.name: ZEUS GMBH, ZENTRUM FUR ANGEWANDTE PSYCHOLOGIE, UMWELT- UND SOZIALFORSCHUNG
items.in_triad: Leads the analysis and evaluation of the pilots, including the co-evaluation workshops with stakeholders (WP6), and the policy recommendations.
items.brings: Psychometrics, large-scale data collection and stakeholder engagement.

items.name: SVEUCILISTE U ZAGREBU, FAKULTET ORGANIZACIJE I INFORMATIKE
items.in_triad: Leads the adoption materials for schools: toolkits, guides and training resources (WP8).
items.brings: Learning analytics, adaptive decision-making, gamification and innovative teaching.

items.name: VERSLO IR SVETINGUMO PROFESINES KARJEROS CENTRAS
items.in_triad: Brings in vocational education and training in Lithuania, so that scenarios and materials also work for VET learners and trainers.
items.brings: Vocational learning environments, and aligning digital competences with career pathways.

items.name: BERUFSBILDUNGSZENTRUM DER KREISHANDWERKERSCHAFT MARKISCHER KREIS - BBZ EV
items.in_triad: Brings in vocational education and training in Germany, so that scenarios and materials also work in VET schools and workshops.
items.brings: Vocational learning environments, with inclusive, practice-oriented training scenarios tested in real VET settings.

intro:
The TRIAD consortium combines universities, a research institute, a consultancy, a school and two vocational education and training (VET) providers. Together the partners cover what is needed to develop, test and scale a framework for competences and well-being with AI in education: research on learning and cognition, artificial intelligence and data, teaching practice, and work with schools and society.

The universities bring the research base, from cognitive science and neuroscience to learning analytics and co-creation methods. The school and the two VET providers make sure the scenarios are designed and tested in real classrooms and workshops, with adolescents who are preparing for the labour market. Each partner leads the part of the work closest to its strengths.
map_text: The classroom pilots run in six countries. The scenarios are first tried out in Croatia, Germany and Greece, and then tested in Lithuania, Germany, Croatia, Finland, Italy and Greece. Partners are based in seven countries; the dots mark their home cities.
